videos.title: Top 3 in the world for typing 🤯
videos.description:
I type at 157 words per minute. That's top 3 in the world (in the last 24 hours, at least).

But speaking is still more than twice as fast 🤯

I raced myself typing vs dictating the exact same message, and typing took ~45 seconds while speaking took about 20 seconds. Even with absurdly fast typing, your voice just wins.

The app I'm using here is Wispr Flow. It's not just raw transcription though. It automatically formats lists, removes ums and ahs, capitalises proper nouns, and even recognises product names and people on your team. Way beyond what built-in dictation like Siri gives you 😂

It works anywhere you can type - Slack, Gmail, Claude, ChatGPT, literally anywhere - and it's on Mac, Windows, iPhone, and Android as well. 

For one month free of Wispr Flow Pro, head to https://ref.wisprflow.ai/ali_instagram

videos.title: Essentials: Tools for Hormone Optimization in Males | Dr. Kyle Gillett
videos.description:
In this Huberman Lab Essentials episode, my guest is Kyle Gillett, MD, a dual board-certified physician in family medicine and obesity medicine, and an expert in hormone optimization. We discuss science-based tools for optimizing male hormones across the lifespan, including the role of bloodwork, nutrition, and exercise in supporting healthy hormone levels. We also discuss testosterone therapy, hair loss, prostate health, and supplements such as creatine, L-carnitine, Tongkat Ali, and Fadogia agrestis.

videos.title: The Reason You Never Feel Good Enough
videos.description:
Stop waiting for permission to build something. Your next revenue stream starts free at https://www.shopify.com/solved

If confidence comes from real evidence, then where does self-esteem fit, and why did an entire generation get it so wrong? In chapter four, Drew and I take a detour into the self-esteem movement, the feel-good experiment that promised to fix everything from crime to school performance and ended up backfiring in ways we're still living with. We get into the California task force that staked millions on proving self-esteem was a social cure-all, why praising kids for who they are instead of what they do breeds fragility and even narcissism rather than real confidence, and the William James insight the whole movement misread. Then we get to the useful part: how you actually build the kind of confidence that generalizes across your life. That's where meta self-efficacy comes in, the quiet belief that whatever happens you can handle it, illustrated by a woman who built a billion-dollar company after getting rejected by every factory she called.
Get your free PDF guide: https://solvedpodcast.com/confidence

This is chapter 4 of our episode on Confidence. New chapters drop every few days. Watch the full episode now on Spotify: https://tinyurl.com/a2fhww9a
